item.title: Measuring Bounded Autonomy for an LLM Decomposition Planner on a Live 5G-Core Testbed
item.description: arXiv:2611.08707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering network-management control loops, yet their plans can fall outside the executable action space. Whether hard deterministic bounds around such a planner have real effect, or merely restate a definition, is an empirical question. We measure it on a live 5G-core testbed, where an LLM planner decides when to decompose control-plane procedures into stateless handlers inside a bounded loop: a JSON schema constrains the output, a projection-repair validator re-checks it, a deterministic fallback guarantees liveness, and every decision is persisted. Three measurements anchor the paper. First, the two tested models, run unbounded with the allowed action sets stated in the prompt, still violated intent-handler rules in 13 of 44 standard calls. Every violation broke an intent-handler combination rule that the deployed flat schema cannot encode (schema enforcement as deployed caught 0/13); a union schema encoding the rule removes the class by construction. Second, with the bounds in place, all 33 decoded live plans were feasible without repair, and a matched-condition probe put the in-distribution unbounded rate at one violation in 20 windows. Third, exploratory: on the design set the planner matched an author-specified selection reference that a threshold policy and three a priori codings each missed. Transfer to held-out scenarios remained partial (5-6 of 10), and the planner's two-clause distillate could replace the runtime planner itself. Together, the results suggest elicitation and distillation, not runtime control, as the LLM's role.
item.dc:creator: Sanjeet Raj Pandey, Axel K\"upper

item.title: Stochastic AI Model Placement for AI-and-RAN Coexistence in 6G Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.08739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers AI-service placement over geographically distributed RAN sites equipped with GPU resources partitioned into fixed, isolated multi-instance GPU (MIG) profiles. We propose C$^2$AIR, a chance-constrained optimization model that maximizes expected AI requests served while protecting uncertain RAN workloads and enforcing probabilistic capacity reliability requirements for admitted AI services. C$^2$AIR allows a service to run at multiple sites and accounts for discrete profile, memory, and GPU-slice constraints. We evaluate C$^2$AIR on a four-site deployment calibrated from NVIDIA Aerial RAN capacity figures and MLPerf Inference results, and on seven larger scenarios with up to 15 sites and 40 AI services, computing every violation and overload probability exactly from the demand distributions. C$^2$AIR keeps the RAN violation probability within its target at every hour of the day, whereas reserving for the mean RAN demand violates it in 24\% to 47\% of the intervals. The reliability condition prevents placing AI models that would be overloaded in 85\% of the intervals at an event hour, and multi-site replication serves 2.7 times more AI requests than single-site deployment. The evaluation also shows that coarse MIG instances and a heavy demand tail can make strict RAN protection expensive.
item.dc:creator: Alaa M. Altarazi, Mohammad J. Abdel-Rahman

item.title: StarLoc: A Practical Approach to Encoding Geographic Locators in IPv6 for Starlink
item.description: arXiv:2611.08772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LEO satellite networks such as Starlink provide Internet connectivity across continents, oceans, and airspace. IP geolocation providers map Starlink's IPv6 prefixes to locations mainly through its self-published GeoFeed. However, users may be far away from their assigned Points of Presence (PoPs), one label covers an entire prefix, and labels and PoP mappings can change while addresses stay the same. We characterize Starlink's IPv6 addressing using 925 historical GeoFeed snapshots (2024--2026), one year of PoP mappings, and over 7.9 million observed IPv6 addresses. Our findings reveal that customer prefixes lack clear geographic structure, prefix labels lie a median of 540km from their PoPs, and relabeling a single /40 can affect the reported locations of up to 65,536 possible /56 delegations. To address these challenges, we propose StarLoc, a geographic Locator--Identifier separation scheme that embeds terminal location into IPv6 addresses using a resolution-adaptive H3 Locator while preserving existing Starlink prefixes, /56 delegations, and stable Endpoint Identifiers. To balance accuracy and privacy, StarLoc reveals only cells with at least a certain number of terminals, and operators can cap resolution in sensitive regions or withhold location entirely. Unlike topology-based schemes, StarLoc encodes physical location and lets Locators follow moving users.
item.dc:creator: Vanya Singla, Mostafa Abdollahi, Jinwei Zhao, Jianping Pan

item.title: Age of Information for Power-Saving Devices with DRX Mechanism
item.description: arXiv:2611.08949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reducing the power consumption of User Equipment (UE) has always been a crucial issue in communication systems. As a result, Discontinuous reception (DRX) is introduced in today's New Radio (NR) networks as a power-saving strategy. In addition, the variety of low latency applications in 6G makes the issue of maintaining data freshness increasingly important. This paper aims to study the relationship between freshness and power-saving. To capture the information freshness, we use Age of Information (AoI) as the performance metric. To our best knowledge, unlike previous studies focusing on power saving and delay trade-offs, this is the first study considering the impact of DRX on AoI. We solve the closed-form solution of the peak average AoI with the DRX mechanism. Moreover, we propose a parameters adjustment strategy. Based on the simulation validation, our proposed strategy can enable the UE to keep the AoI close to the theoretical lower bound AoI while achieving high power-saving efficiency.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: ICC 2023 - IEEE International Conference on Communications, pp. 3234-3239, 2023
item.dc:creator: Hung-Chun Lin, Kuang-Hsun Lin, Hung-Yu Wei

item.title: Adaptive Age of Information Optimization in Rateless Coding-Based Multicast-Enabled Sensor Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.08970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As the demand for real-time information in Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) scenarios grows with the evolution of bandwidth-intensive 5G applications, multicast transmission becomes increasingly vital. This paper delves into the significant role of multicast in WSN, exploring a novel perspective of using rateless codes over the traditionally employed Hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) for eliminating retransmissions in a wireless multicast system. We aim to optimize data freshness, quantified by the Age of Information (AoI), and analyze strategies to minimize time-average AoI in a multicast environment with diverse channel conditions. Specifically, our policy focuses on optimizing the time-average AoI based on sensor devices' feedback. We transform the problem into a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to locate optimal and low-complexity suboptimal policies. We present the first age-minimum scheme for rateless code-based wireless multicast systems. Our numerical simulations reveal that the proposed policies, developed considering unique system structural properties, consistently surpass baseline strategies. We are thus able to preempt updates at the most beneficial time, thereby addressing the issue of the bottleneck device's adverse impact on overall performance.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Journal of Selected Areas in Sensors, vol. 1, pp. 73-92, 2024
item.dc:creator: Hung-Chun Lin, Kuang-Hsun Lin, Hung-Yu Wei

item.title: Computation-Efficient Aerial-Marine Integrated Networks for Search and Rescue via Cooperative HAPS, UAVs, and MASSs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose an aerial-marine integrated network architecture tailored for maritime search and rescue (MSAR) operations, where a high altitude platform station (HAPS) and maritime autonomous surface ships (MASSs) are equipped with edge servers, providing computing services for surveillance uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). These UAVs generate substantial volumes of computation-intensive and delay sensitive tasks, some of which can be strategically offloaded to both MASSs and HAPSs for distributed processing. We formulate the joint task offloading and resource allocation as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) to minimize the system computation overhead (CO), quantified by a weighted sum of task completion time and energy consumption. Given the stochastic nature of task arrivals from UAVs and the dynamic characteristics of marine channel conditions, we employ a two-stage optimization to decompose the problem into four tractable subproblems, i.e., 1) edge server selection, 2) transmission power allocation, 3) edge computing resource allocation, and 4) local computation resource allocation. In stage I, we optimize the edge server selection via many-to-one matching. In stage II, we determine the transmission power of each UAV with quasi-convex optimization and solve the edge computing and local computing resource allocation subproblems via a projected gradient descent method and convex optimization, respectively. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme can achieve superior system performance over benchmark schemes.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Wang, Bin Lin, Qiang Ye

item.title: An Empirical Evaluation of a Weighted PALU Model for Internet Traffic Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.09575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The PALU model is a hybrid power law generative framework that decomposes Internet traffic graphs into three structural components: a preferential attachment core, degree one leaf nodes, and disconnected satellite clusters. Although the original PALU formulation provided a theoretical basis for this decomposition, it was never validated against real traffic data and was restricted to unweighted networks. This work presents the first empirical evaluation of PALU against real Internet traffic, using packet traces from the MAWI WIDE samplepoint F dataset. We introduce a weighted extension of the model incorporating strength degree scaling, and develop a packet-to-graph pipeline for parameter estimation across multiple observation window sizes. Results show that the power law degree exponent $\alpha \approx 2.0$ remains stable across observation scales from $10^5$ to $3 \times 10^6$ packets, consistent with the PALU structural prediction. However, the satellite cluster parameter $\lambda$ and the weighted scaling parameter $\theta$ exhibit systematic dependence on observation scale, and the Poisson star assumption for unattached components is formally rejected at all tested window sizes. These results indicate that PALU captures important aspects of Internet traffic structure but requires an explicit observation model to fully account for finite sampling effects.
item.dc:creator: Wood Moore, Hayden Jananthan, Jeremy Kepner

item.title: Scalable Full-Horizon SFC Deployment over Predictable SAGIN Topologies via Configurable Column Generation Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.09585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) integrate heterogeneous communication and computing resources to support ubiquitous services. Service function chains (SFCs) enable complex services to be composed of ordered functions and executed collaboratively across these resources. Mobility continuously reshapes connectivity throughout service execution, yet much of the resulting topology evolution is predictable. Decisions based only on isolated topology snapshots may therefore overlook valuable future connectivity. We formulate an admission-first, cost-aware model on a time-expanded graph for SFC deployment. Our key observation is that temporal feasibility is request-specific, whereas global coupling arises mainly from shared-resource competition. We therefore develop a configurable column-generation framework in which complete request deployments form columns and a restricted master problem coordinates admission and resources. SAGINFE, a fast constructive heuristic built on per-flow embedding (PFE), supplies a standalone feasible solution and initial columns. Configurable pricing schedules combine early-terminated and stricter searches, supplemented by selective PFE candidates. Candidates undergo feasibility and exact reduced-cost checks. Request-wise pricing can run in parallel, followed by finite-pool integer selection. The default configuration improves the admission-first objective over initialization on all 120 main instances. Four pricing workers achieve up to a 2.69-fold median pricing-stage speedup while preserving admitted request counts in the tested cases.
item.dc:creator: Hang Li, Hao Huang, Yihu Xu, Zixuan Kong, Yanling Jin

item.title: 5G-NetBotSim: A Synchronized Co-Simulation Framework for Connected Robots over ROS and srsRAN-based 5G Network
item.description: arXiv:2611.09735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Connected robotic applications increasingly rely on wireless communication for teleoperation, coordination, and distributed autonomy. However, robotic simulators often use ideal links or abstract delay models that do not capture cellular scheduling and protocol processing effects. We present 5G NetBotSim, a realtime co simulation framework integrating ROS/Gazebo workloads with an executable, full stack srsRAN 5G network emulator. The framework provides isolated User Equipment (UE) robot contexts and stage level timing across the host, gNB, UE, ROS, and robot execution stages. We evaluate human to robot teleoperation and robot to robot leader follower coordination under controlled channel quality conditions. Results show how CQI and MCS variations propagate to throughput, communication latency, and robot performance. In leader follower coordination, higher channel quality reduces mean tracking error from 0.558 m to 0.460 m, a 17.6% reduction. These results demonstrate protocol stack in the loop co simulation for joint network and robotic-application evaluation.
item.dc:creator: Narges Golmohammadi, Bhaskara Venkata Raju Garuda, Ayan Joshi, Sabur Baidya

item.title: Link-Level Performance Comparison of 5G Beamforming: Reciprocity-Based SVD vs. Codebook-Based Precoding
item.description: arXiv:2611.09763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Downlink (DL) precoding in mid-band MIMO relies on uplink (UL) sounding reference signals (SRS) with reciprocity-based singular value decomposition (SVD) or channel state information reference signals (CSI-RS) with codebook-based precoding matrix indicator (PMI) feedback. Although SVD precoding offers unquantized beamforming, it depends on a channel estimate from SRS transmitted at the limited user equipment (UE) power, whereas Type-I PMI is quantized but derived from a high-power CSI-RS based channel estimate. In this paper, we compare SRS-SVD and CSIRS-PMI for single-user MIMO through an end-to-end, 3GPP-compliant link-level simulation at 3.75 GHz with 100 MHz bandwidth, using a 192 antenna element gNB mapped into 32 ports, the 3GPP Release 19 UE antenna model, and ray-traced (RT) channels in Manhattan and Chicago. We show that neither scheme is uniformly superior: CSIRS-PMI serves weak and shadowed users better and reduces outage, whereas SRS-SVD achieves higher spectral efficiency (SE) and enables more multi-layer transmission for users with strong channels. The results on the Clustered Delay Line (CDL)-C statistical channel also confirm this crossover. We further show that by utilizing a simple logistic regression based on the received power of the standard CSI reference signal (CSI-RSRP) and the channel quality indicator (CQI), the gNB can select the optimal transmission scheme with around 90% accuracy, achieving an SE that closely approaches an ideal per-user selection.
item.dc:creator: S. M. Haider Ali Shuvo, Seda Dogan-Tusha, Monisha Ghosh

item.title: VLA Handover: Failure-Prediction-Based Switching from On-Robot to Server VLA Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.08987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large vision-language-action (VLA) models generalize well but are difficult to run in real time on a robot, and small VLAs that run there fail more often. Remote inference over beyond-5G and 6G networks lets a robot use a large VLA on a server, but querying the server for every action chunk limits the number of robots per server. We propose VLA handover: the robot runs a small VLA (S-VLA) and switches to a large VLA (L-VLA) on a server only when the S-VLA is likely to fail. We formulate the switching as minimizing the request cost under a required success probability and, since this problem cannot be solved directly, propose a heuristic framework that retrains neither VLA. In simulation with SmolVLA and $\pi_{0.5}$ on three of the four LIBERO suites, VLA handover raised the success rate by 11-22 percentage points over the S-VLA alone and sent 49-77% fewer requests than server-only control at a 2-4 percentage-point lower success rate, and its completion time grew less with the network latency.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Nishio

item.title: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
item.description: arXiv:2611.09451v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.
item.dc:creator: Jorg Wieme, Eli De Poorter, Jeroen Hoebeke

item.title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Soprana, Michael Stocker, Davide Vecchia, Matteo Trobinger, Carlo Alberto Boano, Gian Pietro Picco

item.title: A Cross-Domain TARA-to-NAC Rule Mapping Methodology: From Automotive OEM Networks to Energy Storage Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threat analysis and risk assessment under ISO/SAE 21434 ends with cybersecurity goals, but existing methods give little structured guidance for turning those goals into enforceable network access control rules. Compliance standards such as IEC 62443, ISO/SAE 21434, and ISO/IEC 27001 are usually applied as parallel efforts rather than as one enforcement architecture. This paper presents a six-step methodology that maps cybersecurity goals from a threat analysis and risk assessment to network access control rules, each placed at a named enforcement point and traceable to the threat records behind it. It also presents a unified compliance framework that treats IEC 62443 and ISO/IEC 27001 as a fixed substrate and domain-specific regulation as an interchangeable overlay. The methodology is applied to an automotive original equipment manufacturer plant network, addressing multi-tier supplier authorization and legacy operational technology devices, and then to utility-scale battery energy storage, where North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection standards and ISO/IEC 27019 replace the automotive-specific standard while the substrate stays constant. In the automotive example, 37 threat entries and 24 cybersecurity goals yield 23 rules covering 11 of the 13 in-scope goals; the energy example yields six rules. Three derived rules have no equivalent in the cited standards. Both examples are desk-based: the methodology is applied to them, not tested on them. The result is a reusable pattern for translating risk assessment into enforcement across critical infrastructure sectors, with empirical validation left as future work.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Teja Medam, Thiago Quinelato

item.title: BRAVR: An AP-Assisted Online DRL Mechanism for Interactive VR Bitrate Adaptation over Wi-Fi
item.description: arXiv:2606.24389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interactive virtual reality (VR) streaming over Wi-Fi requires stringent latency and reliability guarantees, which become increasingly difficult to achieve under dynamic channel conditions and shared-medium contention. These challenges make real-time bitrate adaptation a critical yet fundamentally difficult control problem, particularly under limited visibility of network conditions. This paper formulates VR bitrate adaptation as a network-aware, online decision-making problem and proposes BRAVR, a decentralized deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm that combines application-layer observations with lightweight wireless statistics collected at the Wi-Fi access point (AP) to balance visual quality, streaming performance, and multi-user airtime fairness. We implement BRAVR in a real VR streaming system and evaluate it on a physical Wi-Fi testbed against the VR-tailored NeSt-VR algorithm and an ablated BRAVR variant without AP telemetry. Experimental results show that, in the evaluated scenarios, BRAVR consistently achieves its design objectives, delivering robust quality of service (QoS) while avoiding sustained airtime overutilization. It also outperforms the AP-blind ablation, demonstrating the value of incorporating network-level information into the bitrate adaptation control loop. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of AP-assisted online learning for decentralized interactive VR streaming over commodity Wi-Fi and provide practical insights into bitrate adaptation in shared wireless environments.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Casasnovas, Francesc Wilhelmi, Boris Bellalta

item.title: A Wavelength Borrowing Architecture for Optical Data Center Networks - Extended Version
item.description: arXiv:2609.04874v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growth of east-west traffic, along with the cost and power consumption of electronic switching, is motivating the integration of a low-power, high-rate, all-optical layer within the data center network. This paper presents a spine-leaf all-optical architecture in which the default wavelength configuration, one wavelength per source--destination leaf pair, can be reconfigured to accommodate unbalanced traffic demand: wavelengths that are unused or lightly loaded at one leaf are borrowed by another leaf with higher demand. This topology-engineering capability is combined with a traffic-engineering scheme, based on two-hop detouring, enabling the control of wavelength load while limiting the amount of detoured traffic. A key feature of the architecture is that its degree of wavelength reconfigurability is set by a single tunable parameter, the borrowing degree $B$, ranging from none to full; performance evaluation shows that performance nearly equal to that of a fully reconfigurable architecture is achieved well below the maximum $B$, saving the complexity of a fully reconfigurable solutions. The optical fabric relies on mature, data-center-grade components, namely AWGs, AWGRs, colorless OXCs, and combiners. The reconfiguration speed and the adopted dynamic control policy make the architecture suitable for network tiers where the traffic varies on timescales of tens of minutes or more, e.g., among groups of racks (pods).
item.dc:creator: Andrea Detti, Chiara Lodovisi, Silvello Betti

item.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21390v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Collaborative edge large language model (LLM) systems often require repeated prefill computation when task contexts are transferred between agents. Reusing previously computed key--value (KV) caches can eliminate this overhead, but requires KV-cache delivery before the receiving agent begins decoding. Under strict deadlines and unreliable edge links, complete KV cache transfer may be infeasible, making the timely delivery of useful KV information critical. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that combines prioritized source transmission with adaptive loss recovery. PriorityFEC first organizes KV blocks into a utility-aware source queue to prioritize important information. It then employs ACK-sliding Streaming FEC and a lightweight Double Deep Q-Network (Double-DQN) scheduler to dynamically balance source delivery and repair transmission under deadline constraints. We implement PriorityFEC in a distributed edge LLM-serving prototype and evaluate it using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple workloads. Experimental results demonstrate that PriorityFEC preserves more useful KV information and achieves substantially higher task accuracy than competing transport schemes, particularly when the deadline is insufficient to deliver the complete KV cache.
item.dc:creator: Han Shen, Qifu Tyler Sun, Fanyang Meng, Ye Wang, Yongsheng Liang
